items.boardQuestion: Which current system deserves fresh investment because it already compounds trust, governance, and procurement leverage?
items.currentPosture: The AI governance and agent-readiness lane already resolves into scorecards, procurement proof, and executive memos.
items.recommendedMove: Fund the AI flagship and treat it as the multiplier for governance, trust, and platform narrative reuse.
items.headline: AI is the clearest fund-now lane because it compounds board trust and cross-functional reuse.
items.narrative: The strongest board story is to keep investing where AI governance already anchors procurement, platform, and diligence outputs instead of letting that lane starve.
items.nextBoardAsk: Approve a priority increase for AI governance, agent readiness, and memo packaging as one flagship operating system.

items.boardQuestion: Which risk-control lane should be protected because it stabilizes multiple exposure narratives at once?
items.currentPosture: Identity proof is live across review, posture, and entitlement lanes, but it still acts as one control spine.
items.recommendedMove: Protect identity evidence funding while trimming only duplicate packaging work around it.
items.headline: Identity should be protected because it carries disproportionate board trust for the rest of the control stack.
items.narrative: The board does not reward cutting the lane that keeps access, device, and remediation evidence coherent. Protect the core and only trim duplicate wrappers.
items.nextBoardAsk: Protect the identity evidence ledger and adjacent control plane while consolidating duplicate review motions.

items.boardQuestion: Which revenue-system motion has the cleanest tie between investment and margin recovery?
items.currentPosture: Revenue infrastructure already exposes leak recovery, experiment proof, and reporting-path uplift.
items.recommendedMove: Fund the revenue lane with the clearest leak-recovery path and let the lower-yield backlog wait.
items.headline: Revenue should be funded where margin recovery is already board-readable, not merely plausible.
items.narrative: This is the easiest story to tell a CFO: fund the lane that already ties operator work to saved spend and cleaner growth math.
items.nextBoardAsk: Approve incremental funding for the revenue infrastructure scorecard and margin leak remediation path.

items.priorityTheme: Hold FinTech until proof quality catches up
items.boardQuestion: Where should we hold investment steady until downside exposure and proof fragmentation improve?
items.currentPosture: Payments, KYC, treasury, and merchant review are live, but the story is still clustered across multiple risk motions.
items.recommendedMove: Hold FinTech expansion flat until reserve, KYC, and merchant proof are cleaner and easier to defend.
items.headline: FinTech should hold for now because the downside clusters faster than the board proof improves.
items.narrative: The disciplined answer is not to cut the lane, but to hold it while the diligence and queue-quality story catches up.
items.nextBoardAsk: Keep FinTech funding flat until reserve exposure, KYC refresh posture, and merchant review timing are less clustered.

items.boardQuestion: Which regulated lane behaves like one working operating system and should be defended from opportunistic cuts?
items.currentPosture: GxP, CAPA, specimen, safety, and narrative review now read as one coherent regulated stack.
items.recommendedMove: Protect the core biotech system and only defer peripheral presentation work if the board wants savings.
items.headline: Biotech should be protected because the regulated system already reads as one defensible story.
items.narrative: The mistake would be harvesting short-term savings from the one regulated lane that already behaves like a mature operating layer.
items.nextBoardAsk: Protect the biotech quality system and approve only narrow follow-on evidence improvements.

items.boardQuestion: Where can we save money by collapsing duplicated proof packaging instead of building another buyer-facing layer?
items.currentPosture: Procurement proof is strong, but multiple trust-answer-packaging motions still overlap before reuse is maximized.
items.recommendedMove: Trim overlapping procurement work and reallocate effort into the reusable answer and evidence core.
items.headline: Procurement is the clearest trim lane because savings are visible without killing the core trust story.
items.narrative: The board story gets stronger when procurement proof reuses itself. The right move is to trim duplicate packaging and keep the trust spine intact.
items.nextBoardAsk: Approve a trim across overlapping procurement wrappers and reallocate savings into reusable trust evidence.
